newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Zeneca wins cancer drug battle in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Britain's Zeneca wins cancer drug battle in U.S..

text.p: British pharmaceuticals company Zeneca Group Plc said on Thursday it had won a patent battle in the U.S. courts over its new prostate cancer drug Casodex.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit rejected a challenge by rival drugs companies Schering Corp of the U.S. and Roussel-Uclaf SA of France, which had accused Zeneca of infringing their joint patent.
The court upheld an earlier decision by the U.S. District Court in the state of Delaware.

Casodex, which was approved in the U.S. in October 1995, is currently used in combination with an older class of prostate cancer drugs known as LHRH agonists. Schering and Roussel Uclaf said Zeneca had infringed their patent on the use of combination therapy, even though Zeneca possessed a licence from Roussel Uclaf.
A further allegation that Zeneca infringed the patent before it got the licence has been sent back to the Delaware District Court, although Zeneca said the claim was of "no commercial significance".
Casodex is one of the biggest potential stars in Zeneca's stable of new products, and is winning more than half of all doctor's precriptions for drugs of its type in the U.S.

Around $35 million of Casodex was sold in the first half of 1996, and Zeneca chief executive David Barnes told Reuters on Wednesday that the product had continued to "make very exciting progress in the second half".
Casodex is currently used to treat men with advanced prostate cancer, although the company is examining whether to administer it to patients at earlier stages of the disease.
Prostate cancer is the most common malignancy among men, with 300,000 new cases diagnosed in the United States every year.
